evidence.requirements: All brief items met. The catalogue matches the brief exactly (app/domain/tastings.ts:12-34). The start page shows title, date and time, price per guest and the literal '<n> seats left' (format.ts:12-14, TastingCard.tsx:29-41, start.jpg). The link text is 'Book <title>' (TastingCard.tsx:56). The form has fields labelled Name, Email and Guests (1-8) and a 'Book' button (book.tsx:103-138). Seats are never oversold (booking-store.ts:75-76). Errors are shown next to each field (Field.tsx:35-41, form.jpg). The confirmation has the heading 'Booking confirmed', the tasting, guests, total price and reference (confirmation.tsx:34-47, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a 'Sign in' button and reads STAFF_PASSWORD (staff-auth.ts:9-13, staff.tsx:107-121). Bookings are grouped by tasting with name, email, guests, reference and a Cancel button, and cancelling frees the seats (staff.tsx:169-230, staff.jpg). Bookings are in memory, PORT is honoured via react-router-serve, and the stack is React plus React Router, Zod and Tailwind. There are clear states for error, success and fully booked tastings, and the e2e tests run in a phone viewport (playwright.config.ts:13).
evidence.correctness: store.book is synchronous: it checks seats and inserts in one step, so seats cannot be oversold under concurrent requests (booking-store.ts:68-90). A route test covers two simultaneous requests for the last seats (book.test.ts:114-125). The action validates against the current seats left and the store re-checks (book.tsx:35-49). Guests must be a whole number from 1 to 8, so 1.5, 2e1 and -1 are rejected (booking-input.ts:14-19). Booking exactly the seats left is accepted. Cancel deletes the booking and frees its seats, and the confirmation for a cancelled booking returns 404 (confirmation.tsx:11). Double submits book once because of a per-render submissionId (booking-store.ts:69-70). A fully booked tasting shows a notice instead of the form (book.tsx:85-88). Missing fields or fields that aren't text are treated as empty (booking-input.ts:51). Dates are formatted without timezone drift (format.ts:17-22). Documented limitation: tastings in the past can still be booked (SPEC.md assumption 2).
evidence.security: The password check compares SHA-256 digests with timingSafeEqual (staff-auth.ts:9-13). An unset password locks everyone out (fail closed). Sessions are server-side ids inside a signed cookie that is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure over HTTPS and lasts 8 hours (staff-auth.ts:73-103, session-registry.ts). Sign-out ends the session on the server (staff.test.ts:181-189). Every cancel POST re-checks the session (staff.tsx:62). Failed sign-ins are throttled (staff-auth.ts:30-58). The CSP uses a per-request nonce, with nosniff and frame denial (security-headers.ts, entry.server.tsx:21-24). Staff pages are no-store (staff.tsx:19-21). Form bodies are capped at 16 KB and read as a bounded stream (read-form.ts). React escapes all output and no dangerouslySetInnerHTML is used. The confirmation page shows no personal data (confirmation.tsx:13). There are no secrets in the code. Minor: the global throttle lets an attacker lock staff out of sign-in for a while; this is documented (README.md:47).
evidence.code_quality: The layout is clear: domain/ (pure logic), .server/ (state and auth), components/, routes/. Names are good. Results are typed unions (BookResult), TypeScript is strict with noUncheckedIndexedAccess (tsconfig.json:23-24), and the files are small. Error handling is deliberate: thrown 404/401/400 responses, and a friendly ErrorBoundary (root.tsx:33-67). Comments are few and explain why, not what (booking-store.ts:32, book.tsx:36). Field and Alert are reused across pages rather than duplicated.
evidence.tests: Vitest covers validation edge cases and boundaries (booking-input.test.ts: 0/1/8/9 guests, emails with umlauts, invisible characters). It covers the store: never oversold, cancel frees seats, references unique, idempotent submits (booking-store.test.ts). It also covers routes (book.test.ts with a concurrency race; staff.test.ts with sign-in, throttle, forged cookie, 401 on cancel, sign-out invalidating the session), the confirmation page (no personal data, 404 after cancel) and a component test (TastingCard.test.tsx). The Playwright e2e tests run on desktop and phone. They cover the full guest flow, keyboard-only booking, inline errors, fully booked state, booking without JavaScript, staff cancel restoring seats, security headers, axe checks and a horizontal-scroll check (e2e/*.spec.ts). test-results/.last-run.json shows the last run passed. Every requirement in the brief maps to a test.
evidence.ux_design: The screenshots show a coherent winery look: cream paper background, burgundy serif headings, date badges and generous spacing (start.jpg). There is a summary error alert plus an inline field error with an icon, and entered values are kept (form.jpg). The confirmation has a clear success banner and a prominent reference (confirmation.jpg). The staff page has tidy grouped tables, '4 of 8 seats booked' counts and an empty state (staff.jpg). There is a fully booked badge and a 'Reserving your seats…' pending state (book.tsx:139-143). Weakness: the staff 'Cancel' deletes a booking at once with no confirmation or undo (staff.tsx:214-225), which is risky for a misclick on a phone.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are tied to inputs through useId. Errors are linked with aria-describedby and aria-invalid (Field.tsx:14-28). The error summary has role=alert, and focus moves to the first invalid field (book.tsx:66-68, 97-101). Focus moves to the status message after a cancel (staff.tsx:139-141). There is a skip link, lang=en and a visible gold focus outline (app.css:55-58). Tap targets are at least 44px (min-h-11/12). Icons are aria-hidden. Staff sections are labelled regions, and the table keeps its semantics in the mobile card layout (staff.tsx:170-230). Cancel buttons are described by the guest's name. Axe WCAG 2.1 AA checks run in e2e (fixtures.ts:62-65). The palette has dark text on cream, which looks like good contrast in the screenshots.
evidence.simplicity: Runtime dependencies are minimal: react, react-router plus serve, zod, isbot and fonts. There is no database or extra state library. Some extra machinery goes beyond the brief: idempotent submissionId handling, a bounded form-body reader, a server-side session registry, a hand-written CSP and nonce, and an X-Forwarded-Proto and allowedActionOrigins setup for running behind a proxy. Each is small and justified, but together they add code a small winery app does not strictly need.
evidence.maintainability: README.md covers setup, environment variables, commands, architecture and decisions; SPEC.md holds contracts, assumptions and the threat model; tasks/ holds the plan. package-lock.json is present, the regression suite is strong, and typecheck and e2e scripts exist. Gaps: there is no CI pipeline (no workflow files in the repo). There is no release or changelog approach beyond version 1.0.0. The runtime is only bounded as engines '>=22' with no .nvmrc, and dependencies use caret ranges. There is no short guide for staff, though the staff UI is simple. ALLOWED_ACTION_ORIGINS is a build-time step needed behind a proxy; it is documented.

strengths: Seat handling is correct and well tested. The synchronous store makes the seat check and insert happen together, double submits book only once, and cancelling frees seats. Unit, route (including a concurrency race) and e2e tests cover every requirement in the brief.

Staff security is solid. Passwords are compared in constant time, sessions are server-side ids in a signed HttpOnly cookie, sign-out ends the session on the server, failed sign-ins are throttled, the CSP uses a nonce, and form bodies are size-limited.

The design looks polished and right for a winery, with strong accessibility: errors linked to their fields, focus management, a skip link, large tap targets, axe checks in e2e, and forms that work without JavaScript.
issues: Staff 'Cancel' deletes a booking immediately with no confirmation or undo (app/routes/staff.tsx:214-225). One misclick, easy on a phone, loses a guest's booking for good.

Maintainability gaps: there is no CI pipeline, no release or changelog approach, the Node version is not pinned (engines '>=22', no .nvmrc), and dependencies use caret ranges. Regressions depend on someone running the tests by hand.

Bookings live only in memory and the sign-in throttle is global. A restart wipes every booking, and anyone can lock staff out of sign-in for 15 minutes. Both are documented, but they are operational risks for a real winery.
review.verdict: This is a complete, correct and carefully secured booking app with a polished, accessible winery design and an unusually thorough test suite that covers every requirement in the brief. It can ship. A confirm step for staff cancellations and a CI pipeline should be added soon after.
